turn.text:
Two companies share public IP 203.0.113.9. Give each its own SSL VPN virtual gateway (ports 4433 and 4434) under separate virtual systems; each user may reach only their own company's resources.

Site notes: both companies share fw's public address 203.0.113.9 (eth2). Tenant A's resources are on eth3 (10.11.0.0/24), tenant B's on eth4 (10.12.0.0/24). There are no vendor virtual systems on this Linux firewall: give each tenant a VRF and its own ocserv instance (ocserv is installed; server certificate /lab/keys/vpn.pem, key /lab/keys/vpn.key). Tenant A: user alice / Alice-Pass, client pool 10.9.10.0/24. Tenant B: user bob / Bob-Pass, client pool 10.9.11.0/24. The device has no systemd: start each daemon directly.
Plan: ip link add vrf-a type vrf table 11; ip link set vrf-a up; ip link set eth3 master vrf-a; ip link add vrf-b type vrf table 12; ip link set vrf-b up; ip link set eth4 master vrf-b; cat > /etc/ocserv/a.conf <<'OCS'; printf '#!/bin/sh
ip link set "$DEVICE" master vrf-a
' > /etc/ocserv/a-vrf.sh; chmod +x /etc/ocserv/a-vrf.sh; printf 'Alice-Pass
Alice-Pass
' | ocpasswd -c /etc/ocserv/a.passwd alice; ocserv -c /etc/ocserv/a.conf; cat > /etc/ocserv/b.conf <<'OCS'
